name: InfiniDB
tagline: Calpont's MySQL-fronted columnar MPP engine; vendor bankrupt in 2014, code lives on as MariaDB ColumnStore.
description: InfiniDB was a column-oriented, massively parallel analytic database from Calpont (later renamed InfiniDB Inc.) of Frisco, Texas. It used MySQL as its SQL front end and connection layer, while its own user and performance modules stored data column by column, skipped unneeded columns and extents, and spread query work across threads and nodes without shared state. A Community Edition appeared around 2009 and the full product went GPL v2 in October 2013, with 4.6.2 in September 2014 as the final release. The company ceased operations and filed for bankruptcy that October. MariaDB forked the code into MariaDB ColumnStore in 2016, which is where the technology is maintained today.
statusNote: InfiniDB Inc. ceased operations and filed for bankruptcy in October 2014; the code continues as MariaDB ColumnStore.

pricing.notes: Commercial subscriptions ended with the company in 2014.

strengths: Column storage with extent elimination for scan-heavy analytics
MySQL front end let existing tools and drivers connect
Shared-nothing MPP design scaled across nodes
weaknesses: Vendor bankrupt since 2014; no fixes or releases
Poor fit for frequent single-row updates
useCases: Maintaining legacy InfiniDB installations during migration
notIdealFor: Any new deployment (use MariaDB ColumnStore, ClickHouse or StarRocks)
